You are a programming expert. 
You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From 90f29f0eada4d60e1f6ae537502ddb2202b9540d Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Vladimir Oltean <vladimir.oltean@nxp.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Jan 2020 19:18:28 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] enetc: Don't print from enetc_sched_speed_set when link goes
 down

It is not an error to unplug a cable from the ENETC port even with TSN
offloads, so don't spam the log with link-related messages from the
tc-taprio offload subsystem, a single notification is sufficient:

[10972.351859] fsl_enetc 0000:00:00.0 eno0: Qbv PSPEED set speed link down.
[10972.360241] fsl_enetc 0000:00:00.0 eno0: Link is Down

Fixes: 2e47cb415f0a ("enetc: update TSN Qbv PSPEED set according to adjust link speed")
Signed-off-by: Vladimir Oltean <vladimir.oltean@nxp.com>
Reviewed-by: Andrew Lunn <andrew@lunn.ch>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>

diff --git a/drivers/net/ethernet/freescale/enetc/enetc_qos.c b/drivers/net/ethernet/freescale/enetc/enetc_qos.c
index 00382b7c5bd8..0c6bf3a55a9a 100644
--- a/drivers/net/ethernet/freescale/enetc/enetc_qos.c
+++ b/drivers/net/ethernet/freescale/enetc/enetc_qos.c
@@ -36,7 +36,6 @@ void enetc_sched_speed_set(struct net_device *ndev)
 	case SPEED_10:
 	default:
 		pspeed = ENETC_PMR_PSPEED_10M;
-		netdev_err(ndev, "Qbv PSPEED set speed link down.\n");
 	}
 
 	priv->speed = speed;
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/net/ethernet/freescale/enetc/enetc_qos.c`**
   - A line of code that logs an error message when the link goes down has been removed. Specifically, the line:
     ```c
     netdev_err(ndev, "Qbv PSPEED set speed link down.\n");
     ```
     was deleted from the `enetc_sched_speed_set` function.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification in `enetc_qos.c` addresses a logging issue related to link status changes. The removed log message was deemed unnecessary and potentially spammy when the link goes down, especially in scenarios where it is not an error to unplug the cable. This change is intended to reduce log clutter and improve the clarity of log messages related to link status, particularly in the context of TSN (Time-Sensitive Networking) offloads. The patch is a response to a previous commit that updated the handling of link speed adjustments, indicating that the logging behavior was not aligned with the intended functionality.

Based on your summary and the commit message in the patch, you need to:

1. analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 
2. output the file name that is most likely to cause the bug. 



Provide a response strictly in the following format:
Root cause:<Root cause>
file:<file name>

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
-		netdev_err(ndev, "Qbv PSPEED set speed link down.\n");
```
Reason:
This line of code logs an error message whenever the link speed is set to a lower value, including when the link goes down. Since unplugging a cable is not an error condition, this results in excessive and misleading log messages that clutter the logs without providing meaningful information.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
-		netdev_err(ndev, "Qbv PSPEED set speed link down.\n");
```
Reason:
By removing this line of code, the unnecessary logging of an error message when the link goes down is eliminated. This prevents spamming the logs with misleading messages, ensuring that only relevant notifications about the link status are logged.
